title: Naming a source root can return 409 "named-root response belongs to a superseded work owner" for the current claim holder
outcome: A root session holding a current claim can name a registered worktree and get a definite result, or a stated supported recovery; a superseded owner's reply never leaves the live owner's naming outcome uncertain.
acceptance: A controlled same-binding regression supersedes the work's local transition after the canonical read and before its result is learned; on the unmodified product it produces the reported 409 for a still-current claim, and the original failing evidence is retained.

Ordinary naming under unchanged claim, connection, runtime and exact pending intent handles that post-read supersession through the existing bounded retry within the original budget; genuinely stale authority remains withheld, and unrelated errors or changed authority cannot authorize another producer write.

Tests distinguish the later failure windows after selection/journal installation and during a kept name, verify their reported state and supported identical-request recovery, and preserve the existing genuinely stale-owner regression; no sleeps, timeout inflation or new authority mechanism is added.

The final exact candidate passes focused behavior checks, the independent Codex/Claude review pair with no outstanding Medium-or-higher findings, and the required full gate before landing; it stays outside the priority joint train.

completion.summary: Naming owner recovery landed in combo26 a06f2c92 after original fail-first witness, focused62PASS, clean member/composite review pairs and DL560/Windows FULL gates.
